title: EMAIL channel webhook verifies the signature, records one receipt and rejects replays
risk: A forged or replayed webhook injects messages or sends duplicate outbound replies, and the customer receives the same answer twice or an attacker acts as the customer.
preconditions: Tenant T1 EMAIL webhook route reachable in namespace run-t1-api-ch-email with the channel secret loaded outside the repo
The provider adapter for mail-sandbox is a test sink recording every call and its idempotency key

inputs.signature_scheme: HMAC-SHA256 over raw body plus timestamp header
inputs.tampered_signature: computed over a different secret with the same body

outbound_message.body: Your order ORD-A-1 shipped and arrives in 3 to 5 business days.

steps.action: Deliver one correctly signed inbound webhook for EMAIL
steps.expected: the delivery is accepted and exactly one receipt is persisted keyed by the provider message id

steps.action: Redeliver the byte-identical webhook with the same provider message id
steps.expected: the replay is deduplicated: still exactly one receipt and no second message, case or customer signal

steps.action: Deliver the same body with a signature computed over a different secret
steps.expected: the webhook is rejected with an authentication error and no receipt, message or side effect is created

steps.action: Send one outbound reply and then retry it with the same idempotency key
steps.expected: the provider test sink observes exactly one outbound send and the receipt references that key

assertions: Exactly one receipt row exists per provider message id after the replay: pg_email_1
The tampered delivery creates zero receipts, zero messages and zero outbound calls
The outbound send count in the provider test sink is exactly one for key ch_email_out_key_1
The receipt belongs to channel EMAIL and no other channel or tenant observes it
forbidden: Processing a webhook whose signature does not verify against the channel secret
Sending the outbound reply a second time when the first provider call already succeeded
evidence: Webhook receipt rows with signature verification result, provider message id and idempotency key
Provider test-sink call log showing one accept, one replay dedupe and zero send for the tampered delivery
cleanup: Delete the run-scoped webhook receipts and message rows under run-t1-api-ch-email; keep the immutable audit entries
automation: Post each webhook variant to the real signature-verifying route with the provider adapter replaced by a test sink; the oracle couples the receipt count with the sink call count.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
